title: Stochastic token emulator and p95 watchdog for core-model TPS suite
creator: Nina Patel
description: Build and onboard a stochastic token-stream emulator alongside a p95 regression watchdog to find regressions in tokens-per-second for our core served models. The goal is to extend the existing microbenchmark family with a flexible load generator that can reproduce realistic token arrival patterns (bursts, long-tail sessions, multi-length prompts) and to add an automated regression detection pipeline that triggers alerts and creates annotated bisect tickets when p95 drifts beyond thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: A flexible token-emulator binary (go/rust/python) that can play back token timelines defined by distributions (Poisson, Pareto, stepped bursts) against hosted and dedicated endpoints.
End-to-end CI job that runs the emulator against a canonical set of core models on every runtime release candidate and records p50/p95/p99 and token/sec metrics.
Regression watchdog in Datadog (or observability stack) that compares current p95 vs baseline and opens ENG tickets with attached traces when drift > 10% for 3 consecutive runs.
Synthetic workload library (json fixtures) that covers short-chat, long-form, code-completion, and multi-turn KV-cache-heavy patterns.
Documentation and runbook describing how to add new models, update distributions, and interpret failed runs.
Baseline artifacts (reference metric vectors) stored in S3 with versioned keys and linked from the job output.
No externally visible customer impact from running the tests (tests use non-production namespaces or isolated dedicated capacity).
proposal:
- Implement the emulator as a small containerized service that accepts a workload definition (timeline + prompt templates) and can target a host:port with configurable concurrency and pacing.
- Provide default workload definitions that are derived from production trace sampling (privacy-preserving aggregates) and from perf lab manual cases.
- Integrate the job into our CI pipeline: nightly for full-suite, and on-release-candidate for fast smoke.
- Hook metrics export to our observability: tokens/sec histogram, request latency percentiles, queue depth, kernel utilization (if available).
- Add a lightweight JS/TS wrapper for running the emulator from dev machines and for reproducing specific incidents.
- Implement a regression detector service that pulls the latest run metrics, compares against a baseline stored in S3, and when thresholds are exceeded: create ENG issue, attach run artifacts, and post to #perf-alerts Slack channel.
runbook:
1) How to start emulator locally: repo/README with docker-compose and sample workload.
2) How to run against staging vs dedicated pools: env vars and credential pointers.
3) How to interpret CI job failures: compare p95 to S3 baseline artifact, check model rollout tags, inspect kernel logs.
4) Escalation: if regression persists across 3 nightly runs, page oncall infra and perf team; create a mitigation branch to pin to previous runtime if needed.
ci_integration: Add two jobs: emulator-nightly (full suite, longer run) and emulator-rc (smoke). Each job uploads metrics to s3://redwood-perf/artifacts/ENG-824531/<run-id>/metrics.json and emits event to perf-regression-lambda. Gate: emulator-rc must pass p95 within 5% of baseline for a release to proceed automatically.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Nina Patel: Kicked off spike to evaluate existing replay harness. Found production trace sampling is sufficient to seed distributions but needs normalization to avoid PII leakage.
2026-02-28 - Marco Rodriguez: Prototype emulator in go; container image builds and runs against local mock endpoints. Need to add KV-cache-aware scripting to simulate cache-warm sequences.
2026-03-03 - Elliot Kim (review): Suggest adding a 'stability mode' that runs long-duration low-concurrency jobs to catch memory growth and drift.
2026-03-08 - Product feedback (Sara Li): Ensure outputs attach model hash and runtime kernel metadata to facilitate bisecting regressions across releases.
2026-03-10 - Marco Rodriguez: Updated acceptance criteria: baseline artifacts must be immutable and signed; regression ticket template added.
notes: We should avoid running full-suite on shared prod clusters; prefer dedicated nightly instances or small dedicated fleet.
Consider adding an option to replay exact token timing from sampled traces (timestamp-level) for incident repros.
Plan to reuse existing metric naming conventions to allow cross-correlation with model rollout metrics.
